blocks.text: The enthalpy of a substance depends not only on its physical state but also on the pressure and temperature, so these conditions must be specified when writing an equation. For accurate comparisons of enthalpy changes, delta H is determined under standard conditions: a temperature of 25 degrees C (298 K) and a pressure of 1 atm (101 kPa).

blocks.title: Did you know
blocks.text: The standard state of an element is its most stable form at 298 K and 1 atm; the standard state of carbon is graphite, not diamond. By definition the standard enthalpy change of formation of any element in its standard state is zero.

blocks.caption: Standard enthalpy changes of this topic
rows: Substance burnt completely in excess oxygen
Gaseous atoms formed from the element
Water formed from an acid and an alkali
Gaseous uni-negative ions from gaseous atoms and electrons

blocks.prompt: Why must enthalpy changes be compared under standard conditions, and what is the standard enthalpy of formation of oxygen gas?
blocks.explanation: Enthalpy depends on temperature, pressure and physical state, so values measured under different conditions cannot be compared; 298 K and 1 atm fix them. Oxygen gas, O2, is the standard state of the element, so its standard enthalpy of formation is zero by definition.

items: Standard conditions: 25 degrees C (298 K) and 1 atm (101 kPa); an element's standard state is its most stable form (graphite for carbon) and its standard enthalpy of formation is zero.
